title: Naming the building ahead no longer pauses the walk on a computer
items: Nothing you can see in the town changed. On a computer, the tag that names the building in front of you made the page wait for the graphics card twice a second while you moved; it now reads its answer a frame or two later instead.
It names the same building at the same distance, a moment later. A click on a building still answers at once.
Phones already named the building ahead without that wait, and are unchanged.
